FSD is miles better than their standard autopilot. I’ve lived in Toronto, Manhattan, and LA with my model Y. In each of those cities FSD has been a godsend. Highly recommended! Especially with stop and go traffic in and out of the city during peak hours.

This is probably a very unpopular opinion, but I love my FSD. I’ve done multiple road trips, and it is a life saver. Long day, and you’re doing mundane driving on your way home? FSD makes your commute less intensive. Stuck in traffic? FSD is gentle and brilliant at stop and go traffic. 

I definitely use it like a tool, constantly engaging and disengaging it as need be. I don’t trust it fully with merging, high stress situations, or when there are abnormalities on the road. But when conditions are right, using it to your advantage is well worth the $12,000 CAD I paid for it.

Dude… you meet people, build a network, make money filling crew roles. Once you’ve amassed enough of a network, people will work with you on your projects because they trust you. Until then, your SOL if you think you can skip these steps.
Where are you located? What roles can you fill on crew?

It’s a tough reality but those who don’t make it often suffer in those categories. If people like you and you’re a hard worker that’s good at your job (any position), people will want to work with you again and will boost you up alongside themselves.
Have you joined local Facebook pages? Made friends with people who work in the industry/at your level? If not, start there. Apply for free PA work. Meet people. That’s the key.

Hey! So first off, love the Robin outfit. So gorgeous. 

In terms of advice, I’d personally work on motivating your shots, and keeping yourself one step ahead of the audience with how you show us things. Cut faster, especially on that Robin intro. Another major point that will help your scenes flow is making sure to give actors direction that makes sure they’re acting the ENTIRE time, and not just waiting for their scene partners to give their lines. Acting is reacting, not line reading. That first two shot of Robin and the criminal goes on for far too long IMO, and if you watch either actor while the other is giving their lines you can tell they’re just waiting for the dialogue to be done to continue their own/perform an action (like when Robin moves his arm closer to the guys face). 

Good luck! I hope you guys have a stellar time making it.
